verdicts.quote: The API accepts 2 different authentication methods: Digest auth (http); Service accounts (oauth2).
verdicts.reason: Vendor docs explicitly support OAuth2 via service accounts (client credentials), which is the likely choice for a multi-tenant agent toolkit.

verdicts.quote: If you haven't already created a service account or API keys for an organization, you can create them for a project to grant that project access to the Atlas Administration API.
verdicts.reason: Credentials (service accounts or API keys) are self‑provisioned in the UI; Atlas also has a free‑forever M0 tier for testing, so working creds are obtainable self‑serve and free.

verdicts.quote: Atlas Administration API resources add, edit, or delete administrative objects within Atlas, including projects, users, and clusters.
verdicts.reason: The reference spans many resource families (orgs, projects, clusters, users, networking, backups, search, streams, teams, etc.), indicating broad coverage across Atlas’ control plane.

verdicts.quote: MongoDB hosts, runs, and maintains the MongoDB MCP Server in Atlas.
verdicts.reason: Confirms an official, vendor‑maintained Atlas Managed MCP Server; the same page also documents a Local MCP option from MongoDB.

verdicts.quote: client ID, provided by MongoDB during onboarding.
verdicts.reason: While you can build today with self‑serve service accounts, the user‑delegated OAuth 2.1 flow (the most user‑friendly path for multi‑tenant apps) requires MongoDB onboarding/partner approval; plus the Admin API is control‑plane only, so data‑plane access needs separate setup.
